$comment: Ten Iowa corn/soybean field operations for the landscape exhibit. Machine geometry sets annual utilization; window_days sets timeliness; the custom_rate_* pair joins into ISU A3-10 for the market-depth overlay; a3_29_machine joins into ISU A3-29 for wearout hours, remaining value and repair factors. nass_series_key names the etl.crop_progress series whose observed spread measures this operation's window; four rows resolve to a series and etl.reference.load_operations replaces their window_days with the NASS-measured value (window_confidence becomes 'measured'); null (six rows: spraying, tillage, fertilizer application) means NASS publishes no progress series for the operation, so window_days stays this file's author estimate - see deliverables/appendix/assumptions.md section 11.1. passes_per_farm_acre_per_year assumes a 50/50 corn-soybean rotation, so corn-only operations carry 0.5; per-row reasoning is in each row's passes_source. useful_life_years is a uniform 10-year author assumption across every row; see each row's life_source.

source.scope: Iowa corn and soybeans. Every cost basis is Iowa-specific; the framework generalises, the numbers do not.

operations.label: Self-propelled sprayer
operations.custom_rate_operation: Ground, broadcast, not incorporated, self-propelled / acre
operations.passes_source: Two herbicide passes per farm acre per year - one pre-emergence burndown, one post-emergence - under the 50/50 corn-soybean rotation stated in the file-level $comment. Both crops receive both passes, so the multiplier is not halved the way the corn-only or soybean-only operations are.
operations.window_source: Post-emergence herbicide labels cap application at weed height (waterhemp 4 in), which in Iowa gives roughly a ten-day usable window. Author estimate; NASS Crop Progress days-suitable replaces it in phase 2.
operations.machine_source: UADA FSA2225 (Sept 2025) base machine: 120 ft boom, 18 mph, 0.75 field efficiency. Same values as engine/models.py; see sources.md section 4.
operations.price_source: UADA FSA2225 (Sept 2025), base self-propelled sprayer. Dated, manual.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: Combine, corn head
operations.passes_source: Corn combining touches only the corn acres - half the farm under the 50/50 corn-soybean rotation stated in the file-level $comment - once per year.
operations.window_source: Iowa corn is harvested over roughly a month as grain moisture falls; standability, not agronomy, sets the deadline. Author estimate.
operations.machine_source: 12-row 30-inch corn head (30 ft) at ASABE D497 typical combine speed and field efficiency.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: Combine, draper head
operations.passes_source: Soybean combining touches only the soybean acres - half the farm under the 50/50 corn-soybean rotation stated in the file-level $comment - once per year.
operations.window_source: Soybeans shatter and pods drop once dry, so the harvest window is materially tighter than corn's. Author estimate.
operations.machine_source: 40 ft draper head at ASABE D497 typical combine speed and field efficiency.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: No-till planter
operations.passes_source: Every farm acre is planted once a year, corn or soybean, so the planter makes one pass per farm acre regardless of the 50/50 rotation split named in the file-level $comment.
operations.window_source: Iowa's optimal corn planting window runs from roughly 20 April into the first week of May; soybeans overlap it. Author estimate.
operations.machine_source: 24-row 30-inch planter (60 ft) at ASABE D497 typical planting speed and field efficiency.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: High-speed planter
operations.passes_source: Same reasoning as the no-till planter: every farm acre is planted once a year, so one pass per farm acre. This row and the no-till planter are alternative machines a farm chooses between for the same planting job, not equipment it runs both of - see assumptions.md section 11.
operations.window_source: Same agronomic window as the conventional planter; the machine buys acres per hour inside it, not more days.
operations.machine_source: 24-row 30-inch high-speed planter (60 ft) at 10 mph, the class's marketed working speed.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: Field cultivator
operations.passes_source: Secondary tillage runs once across the whole farm ahead of planting, corn and soybean ground alike, so one pass per farm acre per year regardless of the 50/50 rotation split.
operations.window_source: Secondary tillage runs immediately ahead of the planter and inherits its window, less the days lost to soil moisture. Author estimate.
operations.machine_source: 50 ft field cultivator at ASABE D497 typical secondary-tillage speed and field efficiency.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: Vertical tillage
operations.passes_source: Spring residue sizing targets corn ground only - half the farm under the 50/50 corn-soybean rotation stated in the file-level $comment - once per year.
operations.window_source: Spring residue sizing ahead of planting; competes for the same days as field cultivation. Author estimate.
operations.machine_source: 35 ft vertical-tillage tool at ASABE D497 typical tillage speed and field efficiency. A3-29 has no vertical-tillage row; Disk is the closest machine class.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: Chisel plow
operations.passes_source: Fall primary tillage follows corn harvest, covering the corn half of the farm under the 50/50 rotation stated in the file-level $comment - one pass per corn acre per year.
operations.window_source: Fall primary tillage runs from harvest to freeze-up - the widest window of any operation here. Author estimate.
operations.machine_source: 30 ft chisel plow at ASABE D497 typical primary-tillage speed and field efficiency.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: Anhydrous applicator
operations.custom_rate_operation: Anhydrous   - injecting, with tool bar / acre
operations.passes_source: Anhydrous ammonia is applied ahead of corn only, covering the corn half of the farm under the 50/50 rotation stated in the file-level $comment - one pass per corn acre per year.
operations.window_source: Fall anhydrous waits for 50F and falling soil temperature and must finish before the ground freezes. Author estimate.
operations.machine_source: 40 ft applicator toolbar at ASABE D497 typical speed and field efficiency. A3-29 has no anhydrous row; Fert. spreader is the closest machine class.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.

operations.label: Dry fertilizer spreader
operations.passes_source: P and K are applied ahead of corn only, covering the corn half of the farm under the 50/50 rotation stated in the file-level $comment - one pass per corn acre per year.
operations.window_source: P and K go on ahead of corn in the fall or early spring; placement is not time-critical within the season. Author estimate.
operations.machine_source: 70 ft floater spread width at ASABE D497 typical speed and field efficiency.
operations.life_source: A 10-year useful life is an author assumption, applied uniformly across every operation in this dataset rather than sourced per machine. It divides ISU A3-29 wearout hours into rated_annual_hours at load time (etl/reference.py) and sets the age at which the A3-29 remaining-value equation is evaluated for salvage_fraction.
